correctness.rationale: The exact lower witness has two mutual distances \(2(\sqrt2-1)\) and four distances \(2\). For the upper bound, each ordered four-edge centroid slice is a compact polytope and the sum of six squared norms is convex, so it suffices to inspect its extreme points. The bundled exact \(\mathbb Q(\sqrt2)\) checker exhausts all rank-one and rank-two slices, covering \(11712\) feasible candidate occurrences, and proves that none exceeds \(40-16\sqrt2\). It separately recomputes \(C'_{\mathrm{NJ}}(X_8)=4-2\sqrt2\) from all \(64\) ordered vertex pairs.

value.rationale: The regular octagon is the canonical eight-vertex centrally symmetric polygonal norm, and \(J_{\mathrm{in}}\) is intrinsically a four-point unit-sphere invariant introduced to measure inscribed quadrilateral geometry. Determining its exact value on this first natural flat-edged regular polygon beyond the square tests whether the defining lower comparison can remain sharp without strict convexity. The answer is structurally informative: equality persists at \(X_8\), so strict convexity is sufficient but not necessary for sharpness at this canonical example.
